comments.body: Temporary pinning to fix CI in https://github.com/google/jax/pull/11220

Located the issue to this line: https://github.com/google/jax/blob/b623ed58b0415f31b4c2f2c389220f1e51de8d93/jax/interpreters/ad.py#L65

In numpy 1.22, `dtype(t) is float0` is True, and in numpy 1.23 `dtype(t) is float0` is False.

This is the operative change in numpy:
```python
import numpy as np
from jax import dtypes
print(np.__version__)
print(np.result_type(dtypes.float0) is dtypes.float0)
```
Before:
```
1.22.4
True
```
After:
```
1.23.0
False
```

I don't know for sure, but I suspect this is the relevant change: https://github.com/numpy/numpy/pull/19345/

Edit: actually, the relevant change is almost certainly this: https://github.com/numpy/numpy/pull/19226 ("API: Fix structured dtype cast-safety, promotion, and comparison")

OK, I think this is the result of the new `ensure_canonical` functionality added in https://github.com/numpy/numpy/pull/19226, along with https://github.com/numpy/numpy/pull/19346 which implements `ensure_canonical` for structured arrays.

Part of the reason I think this is because of this little quirk:
```python
In [1]: from jax.dtypes import float0                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            

In [2]: import numpy as np                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       

In [3]: np.result_type(float0) is float0                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         
Out[3]: False

In [4]: np.result_type(float0, float0) is float0                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 
Out[4]: True
```
Along with the fact that `NPY_DT_CALL_ensure_canonical` is only called on the result for the single-input case: https://github.com/numpy/numpy/blob/89b942e41b45ddd91762e704d3f2ca5677a320b7/numpy/core/src/multiarray/convert_datatype.c#L1633

I'm not sure exactly the mechanism whereby this generates a copy, but it seems clear that the fix could go one of two ways:

1. Somehow change our definition of `float0` so it is in a canonical form that doesn't generate a copy when `NPY_DT_CALL_ensure_canonical` is called, or
2. Stop relying on `is` identity to determine if a dtype is equal to `float0`

Option 2 is probably safer in the long run, as I can find no explicit guarantee that functions like `np.dtype` and `np.result_type` will return no-copy references for non-built-in dtypes. However, equality checks for numpy dtypes are annoyingly polymorphic, so this must be used with care (probably `dtype is float0` should be replaced with `np.dtype(dtype) == float0` for safety). Also, since equality check is slightly more expensive than identity check, and since this is used so often throughout the JAX package, this change may have a trace-time performance impact.

I'm going to look deeper and try to find exactly where the copy is being generated, but unless something else comes to light, I think option 2 is our best bet.

I believe the `ensure_canonical` check for void types leads to this function: https://github.com/numpy/numpy/blob/d4baf3641471971552206b02f94323a54b54d99a/numpy/core/src/multiarray/dtypemeta.c#L295 which ends up generating a copy for JAX's definition of `float0`. This was changed a few months back in https://github.com/numpy/numpy/pull/19346

Here's the TODO that broke our use-case: https://github.com/numpy/numpy/blame/d4baf3641471971552206b02f94323a54b54d99a/numpy/core/src/multiarray/dtypemeta.c#L324-L325

I don't see any way for us to prevent copy on dtype canonicalization, unless we define `float0` as something other than a structured void dtype.

Additionally, there are at least two regressions in numpy v1.23 that are causing test failures in the JAX test suite: https://github.com/numpy/numpy/issues/21838 and https://github.com/numpy/numpy/issues/21840
If anyone encounters this, the fix was part of JAX v0.3.14.

issue.body:
# Description

This affects situations where a user explicitly specifies the `backend` argument and uses a tensor for `integration_domain` at the same time.
* If the `integration_domain`'s backend does not correspond to the `backend` argument value, prefer the `backend` argument and show a warning.
  In this case the `integration_domain`'s dtype is ignored, so a globally configured dtype is used instead.
* If the `integration_domain`'s backend corresponds to the `backend` argument value, ignore the `backend` argument.
  In this case the `integration_domain`'s dtype is used and a globally configured dtype is ignored.


## Resolved Issues

-  fixes #153

## How Has This Been Tested?

-  Additional tests in `utils_integration_test.py`

issue.title: Make JAX compatible with numpy version 1.23.0

issue.body:
```python
import jax
import jax.numpy as jnp

def f(x):
    return x + 0.0

def _print_type(x):
    print(x)
    print(x.dtype)
    print(x.dtype is jax.dtypes.float0)

def print_type(x):
    _print_type(x)
    jax.jit(_print_type)(x)
    print("")

x = jax.grad(f, allow_int=True)(jnp.array(1))
y = jnp.array(False)

print_type(x)
print_type(y)
```

With numpy v1.23.0:
```
False
bool
False
Traced<ShapedArray(void[])>with<DynamicJaxprTrace(level=0/1)>
[('float0', 'V')]
False

False
bool
False
Traced<ShapedArray(bool[])>with<DynamicJaxprTrace(level=0/1)>
bool
False
```
Which has the following problems:
- The "outside jit" dtype of `x` is `bool` instead of `float0`.
- The "inside jit" dtype of `x` and `y` are different, despite having the same "outside jit" dtype.
- The "inside jit" comparison of `x.dtype is jax.dtypes.float0` returns `False` despite the "inside jit" dtype of `x` being `float0`. (Probably something to do with it secretly being a `bool` instead.)

This plays merry havoc will all kinds of other things. I spotted this because it was sneaking past the `_check_no_float0s` checker when calling `jnp.allclose`. It also means that attempting to do `x == y` in the above code will result in an exception being thrown.

For reference I've found that numpy v1.21.2 works fine.

Possibly this is a numpy bug? (I did check to see that there weren't any `float0`-related numpy bugs reported.)

I'm experiencing some type promotion errors after upgrading to `numpy==1.23.0`. I'm guessing it's probably not fully supported yet---my current JAX version is `0.3.13`.

The following is a basic repro to trigger the error:

```python
import jax
import jax.numpy as jnp

jax.grad(lambda x: jnp.sum(jax.nn.softplus(x)))(jnp.array([1.0, 2.0, 3.0]))
```

```
    return _promote_shapes(fun_name, *_promote_dtypes_inexact(*args))

    to_dtype, weak_type = dtypes._lattice_result_type(*args)
KeyError: dtype([('float0', 'V')])
```

Note from the stacktrace I thought the culprit would be from `logaddexp`, so I tried:

